readings: For each film rating, compute the average replacement cost and the average of each film's own per-day rate (film.rental_rate divided by film.rental_duration, averaged over the films in that rating). Take the simple unweighted mean of those per-rating per-day averages across all 5 ratings. Keep the ratings whose per-day average is above that mean. Return one row for those ratings: the mean of their per-rating average replacement costs, the mean of their per-rating per-day averages, and the mean amount by which their per-day averages exceed the cross-rating mean. Don't round.

For each film rating, compute the average replacement cost and the per-day rate as the rating's average rental_rate divided by its average rental_duration (ratio of averages). Take the simple unweighted mean of those per-rating per-day rates across all 5 ratings. Keep the ratings whose per-day rate is above that mean. Return one row for those ratings: the mean of their per-rating average replacement costs, the mean of their per-rating per-day rates, and the mean amount by which their per-day rates exceed the cross-rating mean. Don't round.
queries:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT rating,
         AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_rc,
         AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_pd
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
),
m AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_pd) AS mean_pd FROM r
)
SELECT AVG(r.avg_rc) AS mean_avg_replacement_cost,
       AVG(r.avg_pd) AS mean_avg_per_day,
       AVG(r.avg_pd - m.mean_pd) AS mean_excess
FROM r, m
WHERE r.avg_pd > m.mean_pd;
WITH r AS (
  SELECT rating,
         AVG(replacement_cost) AS avg_rc,
         AVG(rental_rate) * 1.0 / AVG(rental_duration) AS pd
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
),
m AS (
  SELECT AVG(pd) AS mean_pd FROM r
)
SELECT AVG(r.avg_rc) AS mean_avg_replacement_cost,
       AVG(r.pd) AS mean_per_day_rate,
       AVG(r.pd - m.mean_pd) AS mean_excess
FROM r, m
WHERE r.pd > m.mean_pd;
